extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners, and USPTO electronic filers using EFS-Web/EFS‑Web Contingency
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and technical rules and quality requirements for preparing, submitting, and validating patent applications and follow-on documents via the USPTO EFS-Web system (including contingency procedures, receipt/filing-date rules, payment methods, and PDF/file-format requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not submit credit/debit card information via EFS-Web
rubrics_metrics.description: Users should not submit a credit/debit card charge authorization including the Credit Card Payment Form (PTO-2038) electronically via EFS-Web, because the electronic submission automatically will be loaded into the application file in IFW, and the credit/debit card information may become part of the record of an application file that is open to public inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit credit/debit card charge authorizations (e.g., PTO-2038) by facsimile to USPTO Central Facsimile (571) 273-8300 or by Priority Mail Express® in accordance with 37 CFR 1.10; include the application number from the Electronic Acknowledgement Receipt to ensure correct payment posting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment of basic national fee for national stage (35 U.S.C. 371)
rubrics_metrics.description: Facsimile submission of the basic national fee for a national stage application under 35 U.S.C. 371 is not accepted; failure to timely pay the basic national fee prior to the expiration of 30 months from the priority date will result in abandonment of the international application for purposes of the U.S. national phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When filing national stage entry, use EFS-Web (if payment systems available), EFS-Web Contingency (if available), or Priority Mail Express/hand delivery per 37 CFR 1.10; do not fax the basic national fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing‑date payment timing to avoid surcharge
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant wishes to submit the application filing fees on the filing date of a patent application to avoid the surcharge, the payment of the filing fees must be submitted and received by the USPTO before midnight ET on the filing date of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternative filing/payment methods (Priority Mail Express, hand delivery) may be used to ensure timely receipt when EFS-Web payment is not available; failure to pay on the filing date will result in a surcharge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submissions requiring online fee payment unavailable when EFS-Web payment down
rubrics_metrics.description: When the online fee payment in EFS-Web is unavailable, certain types of submissions that require a fee for auto-processing by EFS-Web cannot be filed via EFS-Web.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include: (1) petitions that require a fee for auto-processing by EFS-Web; (2) pre-grant publication submissions under 37 CFR 1.211–1.221 that require a fee; (3) third-party preissuance submissions under 37 CFR 1.290 that require a fee; and (4) Web-based Issue Fee Payment (Web 85b). Use alternative filing/payment methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic Acknowledgement Receipt establishes USPTO date of receipt
rubrics_metrics.description: The Electronic Acknowledgement Receipt establishes the date of receipt by the USPTO of documents submitted via EFS-Web and contains a full listing of the documents submitted (including page counts and byte sizes) as described by the user.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Electronic Acknowledgement Receipt is the electronic equivalent of the postcard receipt described in MPEP § 503 and is used to determine filing/receipt dates assuming the submitted documents are entitled to a filing date after review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official filing date determined after USPTO review
rubrics_metrics.description: The official application filing date will be noted on the filing receipt (37 CFR 1.54) after the submitted application parts are reviewed for compliance with 35 U.S.C. 111 (or 35 U.S.C. 371 for national stage). The filing date of an EFS-Web filing is based on the dates indicated on the Electronic Acknowledgement Receipt assuming the documents are entitled to an application filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing receipt (and thus official filing date) may differ from E-Ack if submitted parts are not compliant on review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lost/damaged/unreadable uploaded documents — resubmission and petition
rubrics_metrics.description: If the official version of any document received by EFS-Web is lost, damaged or rendered unreadable and cannot be recovered, the user will be notified and may have to resubmit the missing document(s) and petition for the original filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resubmission petition must present: (1) the Electronic Acknowledgement Receipt; (2) a copy of the missing files as submitted; and (3) a signed petition statement that the attached files are the same as originally submitted. Petition may be under 37 CFR 1.53(e) or 1.182 with appropriate fee under 37 CFR 1.17(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic Acknowledgement Receipt as prima facie evidence (with limitation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Electronic Acknowledgement Receipt and statement will serve as prima facie evidence that the resubmitted documents are the same as those submitted on the date of receipt, except when the document description used by the user does not match the document actually sent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E-Ack indicates only what was received, not what the filer intended; users must exercise care in preparing and preserving copies of electronic submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date of receipt for follow-on documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow-on documents filed after the initial filing will be accorded a receipt date equal to the date the follow-on document is received at the USPTO (see 37 CFR 1.6(a)(4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A follow-on document required to be filed within a set period (e.g., reply to Office action) will be timely if submitted via EFS-Web prior to expiration and (1) complies with EFS-Web requirements and (2) includes a certificate of transmission stating the date of transmission and signed by a person with reasonable basis to expect transmission on or before that date (37 CFR 1.8(a)). Note: the certificate of transmission practice does not apply to documents listed in 37 CFR 1.8(a)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date/time = Eastern Time at USPTO when SUBMIT clicked
rubrics_metrics.description: The time and date of receipt for an application filed via EFS-Web is the local time and date in USPTO headquarters in Alexandria, Virginia (Eastern Time) on which the USPTO receives the documents after the user clicks the SUBMIT button.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants in other time zones should note that an applicant clicking SUBMIT late in their local day may receive the next-day Eastern Time filing date. There is no 'certificate of transmission' practice for new application filings (37 CFR 1.8).

rubrics_metrics.name: EFS-Web hours of operation and assignment of receipt date
rubrics_metrics.description: Hours of operation for EFS-Web are provided in the EFS-Web instructions; users may file electronically every day of the week, including weekends and holidays. If a submission is successfully received, the USPTO will assign that receipt date to the submission (even on weekends/holidays).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO will post scheduled downtime in advance; if system unavailable, USPTO will advise alternative filing methods to establish a filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: If EFS-Web unavailable, use alternative filing methods promptly
rubrics_metrics.description: If a transmission is attempted during downtime, the USPTO cannot accept it and will, if possible, notify the user to use alternative filing methods (Priority Mail Express, hand delivery) in accordance with 37 CFR 1.10 to establish the filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some items (applications filed under 37 CFR 1.53, PCT international applications, international design applications, reexamination requests) cannot be submitted by facsimile transmission and certificate of mailing does not apply to new applications; users are strongly advised to transmit sufficiently early to allow alternative paper filing if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: EFS-Web Contingency option during unscheduled primary portal outage
rubrics_metrics.description: When the primary portal to EFS-Web is unavailable, the USPTO will provide an EFS-Web Contingency option that permits unregistered users to file new applications, certain national stage submissions under 35 U.S.C. 371, reexamination and supplemental examination requests, and certain petitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EFS-Web Contingency provides similar functionality and an Electronic Acknowledgement Receipt; it has limited functionality and does not permit follow-on documents (amendments/replies) after initial submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations of EFS-Web Contingency (no follow-on documents)
rubrics_metrics.description: EFS-Web Contingency (and EFS-Web for unregistered users) does not permit users to file follow-on documents and follow-on fee payments after the initial submission of the application, reexamination request, or supplemental examination request (e.g., amendments and replies to Office actions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If systems EFS-Web Contingency depends on are unavailable (payment processing, PALM), certain features will be unavailable — e.g., online payment option or national stage filing capability.

rubrics_metrics.name: EFS-Web Contingency allowed filing types (enumerated list)
rubrics_metrics.description: EFS-Web Contingency only permits electronic filing of a specific list of items (provisional applications; nonprovisional utility applications; nonprovisional design applications; PCT international applications filed in US Receiving Office; national stage submissions under 35 U.S.C. 371; international design applications under Hague Geneva Act; requests for ex parte reexamination; requests for supplemental examination; certain ePetitions such as petitions to make special based on age and petitions to accept unintentionally delayed maintenance fee payment; petition to make special under accelerated examination with a nonprovisional utility application; reissue applications; third‑party preissuance submissions and 37 CFR 1.501 citations via dedicated interfaces).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each permitted submission must meet the same file format and PDF embedded-font/size/validation requirements as normal EFS-Web submissions; dedicated interfaces may prevent direct placement into the application file for some third-party submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: File format, size, and PDF validation requirements for EFS-Web Contingency
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents filed via EFS-Web Contingency must meet the same file format requirements established for EFS-Web (file size, PDF embedded-font requirements) and the same file validation will be performed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EFS-Web Contingency issues an Electronic Acknowledgement Receipt that establishes date of receipt; do not resubmit when primary portal is restored — resubmission creates duplicate applications and duplicate fees (no refund for duplicate filing fees).

rubrics_metrics.name: Security of EFS-Web Contingency
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications filed via EFS-Web Contingency are protected with the same level of security as EFS-Web for unregistered users by using Transport Layer Security (TLS) to encrypt transmission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registered users who uploaded documents to Saved Submission in EFS-Web will not be able to access those Saved Submission documents through EFS-Web Contingency.

rubrics_metrics.name: PALM checks for national stage submissions and dependency on PALM availability
rubrics_metrics.description: For any national stage submission under 35 U.S.C. 371 filed via EFS-Web or EFS-Web Contingency, the system automatically checks the PALM database to verify that no previous national stage submission has been made for the referenced PCT application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If PALM is unavailable, neither EFS-Web nor Contingency can complete the verification and will not permit national stage submissions; applicants must use hand-delivery or Priority Mail Express per 37 CFR 1.10 to submit national stage documents/fees. National stage cannot be filed by facsimile transmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment alternatives when online payment is unavailable for national stage entry
rubrics_metrics.description: If the USPTO payment system is unavailable, EFS-Web and Contingency will not permit online payment of the basic national fee; applicant may include a written authorization to charge a deposit account with the national stage submission or send payment via Priority Mail Express on the same date the national stage submission is electronically filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the national stage basic fee is received the same date as the electronic submission to establish proper national-stage entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improperly filing follow-on documents as new applications — corrective petition required
rubrics_metrics.description: It is improper for registered and unregistered users to file follow-on documents as new applications. When an applicant improperly files a follow-on document as a new application and wishes the USPTO to move the follow-on document to an intended application, a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 accompanied by the petition fee under 37 CFR 1.17(f) will be required in the intended application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users are encouraged to check USPTO website FAQs and to contact the Patent Electronic Business Center for assistance to avoid improper filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedy and effects of filing a second application to correct an error
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant files a second application to correct an error in the first application, applicant will have filed two applications. Applicant may continue to prosecute the first application that has the error or abandon the first application by filing a petition for express abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees paid in the first application will not be refunded or applied to the second (applicants may request refund of the search fee and any excess claims fees, but not the basic filing fee, examination fee, and application size fee, under certain conditions and per 37 CFR 1.138(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Same-day filing of omitted items for registered users (considered part of original disclosure)
rubrics_metrics.description: A registered user may view their submission in Private PAIR and file a missing item(s) on the same day as the filing date of the application via EFS-Web; certain items filed the same day will be considered part of the original disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (1) executed oath or declaration filed same day will not be considered late; (2) filing fees filed same day will not be considered late; (3) missing drawings filed as a preliminary amendment same day will be part of original disclosure (37 CFR 1.115(a)(1)); (4) claims or missing portions of the written description filed as preliminary amendment on the filing date will be considered part of original disclosure. Nonpublication requests, however, must be filed with the application and cannot be simply filed afterward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonpublication request omitted — special procedure to avoid publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Because 37 CFR 1.213(a)(1) requires any nonpublication request to be filed with the application, an omitted nonpublication request cannot simply be filed later to prevent publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant does not wish publication, they must (a) file a new application with a nonpublication request; and (b) in the initial application, file a petition for express abandonment under 37 CFR 1.138(c) and pay the fee under 37 CFR 1.17(h) in sufficient time to remove the application from publication processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal consequences for weekend/holiday electronic filings and foreign priority
rubrics_metrics.description: Under U.S. law (35 U.S.C. 21(b) and 119(e)(3)), applicants may take action or pay a fee on the next business day if the deadline falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or Federal holiday within the District of Columbia; this applies regardless of filing mode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, Article 4(C)(3) of the Paris Convention may treat the office in the country where protection is claimed as closed on weekends/holidays differently; electronic filing on weekends/holidays in the USPTO could result in loss of priority rights in foreign jurisdictions that interpret Article 4(C)(3) strictly. Applicants filing international or international design applications should consider filing before the Paris Convention priority period expires rather than relying on 'next business day' extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper usage of EFS-Web — check everything before clicking SUBMIT
rubrics_metrics.description: Users should follow EFS-Web instructions and check whether the correct documents have been attached and information entered correctly before clicking SUBMIT. Once SUBMIT is clicked the submission is electronically sent and officially filed when received by the USPTO (Eastern Time).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of EFS-Web in a manner significantly in violation of instructions may result in non-entry or failure to accord a filing date. Electronic files must be free of executables, worms, viruses, or malicious content; intentional damage to federal computers is prohibited under 18 U.S.C. 1030.

rubrics_metrics.name: PDF file requirements: size, count, resolution, and PDF feature limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: EFS-Web accepts standard PDF documents up to 25 megabytes per file and up to 60 electronic files per submission (with exceptions for international design applications). PDF files created from scanned documents must use scanning resolution of no lower than 300 dpi; certain PDF features are not supported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unsupported features include multiple layers (must be flattened) and PDF comments/annotations (information entered as annotations may not be processed — only the blank form is processed). Low-resolution scans have caused processing/publication delays and resubmissions. Users must follow USPTO PDF Guidelines and PDF Creation for EFS-Web.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enter correct metadata and document descriptions in EFS-Web interfaces
rubrics_metrics.description: EFS-Web collects on-screen entries that the USPTO systems use to assign application numbers, upload files into the specified application, or message deciding officials; providing incorrect information can cause incorrect application creation, processing delays, documents filed in the wrong application, or failure to avoid publication/abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When filing a new application, select the correct application type so only pertinent document descriptions and fee codes are available and the system generates the correct application number and processing (e.g., provisional vs nonprovisional). For follow-on documents, enter the correct application number, control/proceeding/confirmation number pair; after submission check PAIR to confirm correct filing. Incorrect filings may require petitions under 37 CFR 1.59 (expunge) or 1.182 (move document) with appropriate fees.
